blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The economy’s “weak” industrial base “limits the creation of stable, productive, and better-paying jobs,” Ibon Foundation said, pointing out that many young Filipinos are unemployed because the economy itself is “failing.” The local think tank made the point as the ongoing reframing of higher education stirs controversy, saying education planners’ focus on whether to invest in so-called human capital for economic competitiveness or develop a wholesome citizenry reflects “an overstated tension.” “It is becoming more apparent that the purpose of reframing is to respond to the evolving demands of the global labor market, particularly the need for a […]...
